symptoms: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers. Neck blast causes blackening of neck node, panicles break and hang down, producing empty chaffy grains.
favorable_weather: High relative humidity (>90%), night temperature 19-23°C, prolonged morning dew (4-6 hours), overcast skies.

symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots on leaves delimited by veins. Lesions coalesce turning reddish-brown to black. Progresses along veins to petioles and stems causing 'black arm', and rotting of young bolls.
favorable_weather: Warm temperature (28-32°C), high humidity (>85%), wind-driven rain showers.

symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' appearance) on lower leaves first. Stem lesions cause collar rot. Sunken leathery dark lesions develop at stem end of fruits.
favorable_weather: Warm temperature (24-29°C), alternating wet and dry periods, heavy dew.

symptoms: Oval or elliptical greenish-grey water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths near waterline. Lesions enlarge and coalesce with irregular snake-skin pattern bordered by dark brown bands. Spreads upward to flag leaves.
favorable_weather: High relative humidity (85-100%), temperature 28-32°C, dense plant canopy, excessive nitrogen fertilizer.

symptoms: Water-soaked streaks starting at leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy yellowish-white lesions that turn greyish-white. Milky bacterial ooze droplets appear on young lesions in morning. 'Kresek' phase causes seedling wilting.
favorable_weather: Temperature 25-34°C, relative humidity >70%, strong winds with continuous rains.

symptoms: Angular, pale translucent spots on lower surface of leaves covered with white powdery frosty growth resembling dusting of wheat flour (dahiya). Leaves turn yellowish brown, curl, dry and drop prematurely.
favorable_weather: Cool night temperatures (20-22°C), high humidity (>80%), cloudy weather in October-November.

pathogen_type: Fungal (Rhizoctonia bataticola & Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum)
symptoms: Sudden wilting of standing plants in patches. Taproot shows shredding of bark, dark brown vascular discoloration, and shedding of lateral fibrous roots. Plants pull out easily from soil.
favorable_weather: High soil temperatures (35-39°C), low soil moisture followed by sudden heavy irrigation, alkaline soils.

name_te: కొమ్మ ఎండు తెగులు మరియు కాయ కుళ్లు
symptoms: Circular sunken spots on ripe red fruits with black concentric rings containing fungal acervuli. Die-back begins as tender twig tips dry backwards from top to bottom, turning dirty white with black dots.
favorable_weather: Temperature 28-30°C, relative humidity >80%, intermittent rain showers after fruit setting.

symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on the lower surface of mature leaves. Upper leaf surface displays corresponding chlorotic yellow patches. Causes severe defoliation leaving bare twigs.
favorable_weather: Warm dry days (25-30°C) with cool humid nights (60-70% RH) in December-February.

pathogen_type: Viral (Chilli leaf curl virus - Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of leaves, thickening of veins, shortened internodes resulting in extreme plant stunting (witches' broom effect). Drastic reduction in flowering and fruit size.
favorable_weather: Dry, hot weather favoring explosive population growth of whitefly vectors.

symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish-brown lesions on leaves and stems. Under humid conditions, white delicate fungal downy growth appears on underside of leaves. Fruits show large, firm, greasy brown sunken blotches.
favorable_weather: Cool temperatures (12-18°C), high relative humidity (>90%), continuous drizzle or persistent fog.

pathogen_type: Viral (Tomato leaf curl virus - Begomovirus vectored by Whitefly)
symptoms: Severe upward and inward leaf curling, interveinal chlorosis, marked reduction in leaf size, bushy stunted appearance. Flowers drop prematurely; no marketable fruit set.
favorable_weather: High temperatures (30-35°C) and low rainfall which favor heavy whitefly breeding.

symptoms: Bright yellow pustules (uredinia) arranged in narrow, parallel linear stripes along leaf veins. Upon rubbing, yellow powder adheres to fingers. Chlorosis and leaf drying follow rapidly.
favorable_weather: Cool humid weather (temperature 10-15°C), intermittent rains, morning dew in North-Western plain zone.
citation: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal Yellow Rust Surveillance Protocol 2025

symptoms: Small, round to oval, orange-brown pustules scattered randomly across leaf blades (not in stripes). Later turn black (telia) as plant approaches maturity.
favorable_weather: Moderate temperature (20-25°C) and high humidity with dew in Central and Peninsular zones.

symptoms: Only a few grains in the earhead are partially converted into black powdery teliospore mass. Diseased grains emit foul fishy odor due to trimethylamine gas.
favorable_weather: Cool cloudy weather, high humidity, light showers during wheat flowering stage (anthesis).

symptoms: Long, elliptical, spindle-shaped greyish-green to tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long) on leaves. Lesions merge causing extensive leaf blighting. Appears first on lower leaves and progresses upward.
favorable_weather: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C), heavy dews, relative humidity >80%.

symptoms: Small, rectangular to oval tan spots with buff to reddish-brown borders strictly confined between leaf veins. Spots coalesce causing premature foliage death.
favorable_weather: Warm temperature (20-30°C) with high relative humidity (>85%).

name_en: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late Leaf Spot)
symptoms: Early spot: Circular brown lesions surrounded by prominent yellow halo. Late spot: Dark carbon-black circular spots without prominent yellow halo on lower leaf surface. Severe premature defoliation leaves naked stems.
favorable_weather: Prolonged leaf wetness, temperature 25-30°C, RH >80% for 3-4 consecutive days.

symptoms: Emerging seedlings collapse and rot at soil line. Collar region covered with profuse black sooty masses of fungal spores. Taproot decays completely.
favorable_weather: Deep sowing, high soil temperature (30-35°C), low soil moisture at seedling stage.

symptoms: Pinhead-sized grey to tan polygonal pustules (uredinia) on underside of leaves. Pustules erupt releasing brown spores; foliage yellows, desiccates and sheds prematurely.
favorable_weather: Moderate temperature (18-26°C), continuous wet weather (>6 hours dew), RH >80%.

pathogen_type: Viral (Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus vectored by Whitefly)
symptoms: Alternating bright yellow and dark green mosaic patches on young trifoliate leaves. Leaves become leathery, puckered; pods remain small with shriveled seeds.
favorable_weather: Dry periods during monsoon promoting rapid whitefly multiplication.

symptoms: Loss of turgidity, wilting and drooping of leaves starting on one side of plant. Splitting the main stem reveals a prominent dark purple-black vascular streak under the bark.
favorable_weather: Soil temperature 20-25°C, continuous cropping of pigeonpea in Vertisols.

pathogen_type: Viral (Pigeonpea sterility mosaic virus vectored by Eriophyid mite Aceria cajani)
symptoms: Bushy stunted growth, mosaic mottling of leaves, total cessation of floral bud formation (sterility). Affected plants stand out green without bearing pods.
favorable_weather: High humidity and warm conditions favoring eriophyid mite populations.

symptoms: Sudden drooping and drying of petiole and pinnae without prior yellowing. Internal vascular tissues turn dark brown to black when taproot is split vertically.
favorable_weather: Warm soil temperatures (above 25°C) at seedling and pod-filling stages, dry soil conditions.

symptoms: White or creamy porcelain-like pustules (blisters) on underside of leaves. Systemic floral infection causes hypertrophied floral malformation known as 'staghead'.
favorable_weather: Cool moist weather (temperature 12-16°C), morning fog and RH >80%.

symptoms: Concentric circular target-board spots on leaves, stems and pods (siliquae). Pod infection results in blackened shriveled seeds and premature shattering.
favorable_weather: Temperature 15-25°C with intermittent showers and overcast sky.

symptoms: Yellowing and withering of third or fourth leaf from crown. Splitting the cane longitudinally reveals crimson-red pith interspersed with characteristic white crosswise bands and alcoholic odor.
favorable_weather: Waterlogged poorly drained soils, continuous ratooning, monsoon floodwaters.

symptoms: Production of a prominent whip-like, curved, pencil-thick unbranched structure (up to 1.5m long) from apical meristem, covered with black sooty chlamydospores.
favorable_weather: Hot dry weather (30-35°C), infected setts, ratoon crops in dry soils.

symptoms: Small, sunken, water-soaked lesions that rapidly expand into large elliptical purple-centered spots with yellow halo on leaves and seed stalks. Stalks break at the lesion.
favorable_weather: Warm temperature (25-30°C), relative humidity >85%, heavy thrips feeding punctures.

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins turning black necrotic; white mildew growth on underside in morning. Tubers develop dry, rusty brown subterranean rot extending into flesh.
favorable_weather: Temperature 10-20°C, RH >90%, persistent dense fog or drizzling rainfall.
citation: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Late Blight Forecasting System 2025

symptoms: Progressive yellowing of lower leaves from margins inwards. Pseudostem collar becomes soft and water-soaked, detaching easily with slight pull. Rhizomes rot into foul soft watery mass.
favorable_weather: Water stagnation, heavy soils with poor drainage, temperature 25-30°C during monsoon.

symptoms: Oblong to circular brown spots with grey center and dark brown margin appearing on both leaf surfaces. In advanced stages, spots coalesce drying out entire leaf lamina.
favorable_weather: High humidity (80-90%), cloudy days, intermittent rains in August-October.
